title: Data partitioning strategies (row, schema, database)
hook: Data partitioning decides how tenant data coexists in storage. Row-level (shared tables), schema-per-tenant, or database-per-tenant each trade isolation, cost, and query complexity differently.

blocks.text: Row-level pooling: one schema, tenant_id column on every table — simplest, highest leak risk if queries miss filter. Schema-per-tenant: separate PostgreSQL schema per tenant — better isolation, migration complexity. Database-per-tenant: separate RDS instance or DynamoDB table per tenant — silo model, enterprise tier. DynamoDB partition key design can embed tenant_id for natural isolation.
Interviewers ask "how do you prevent cross-tenant data leaks in a pooled database?" and "when move enterprise customer to dedicated DB?" Partitioning strategy is the answer.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: row pool for scale, schema/db per tenant for isolation, DynamoDB tenant in partition key.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Choose default strategy
items.body: Row-level pool for freemium; document upgrade triggers.

items.title: Enforce query scoping
items.body: ORM global filter, Row Level Security (RLS) in PostgreSQL, code review rules.

items.title: Plan silo migration
items.body: pg_dump tenant schema → restore to dedicated RDS; dual-write cutover.

items.title: Design DynamoDB keys
items.body: Tenant prefix in pk: TENANT#<id>#ENTITY#<id> for natural isolation.

snippet.label: PostgreSQL Row Level Security
snippet.explanation: DB-enforced isolation even if app forgets WHERE clause.

snippet.label: Schema per tenant
snippet.code:
CREATE SCHEMA tenant_acme;
CREATE TABLE tenant_acme.orders (order_id UUID, amount DECIMAL);
snippet.explanation: Namespace isolation — migration scripts run per schema.

snippet.label: DynamoDB tenant partition key
snippet.explanation: Tenant in pk prevents cross-tenant GetItem without knowing key.

snippet.label: Export tenant schema for silo migration
snippet.code:
pg_dump -h pooled-db -n tenant_acme -Fc -f acme.dump
pg_restore -h acme-dedicated-db -d acme acme.dump
snippet.explanation: Bridge model: migrate enterprise from pool schema to dedicated DB.

blocks.title: Cloud vs app patterns
rows: DB per tenant ops at 10k tenants

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: ORM query without tenant filter — classic data leak. Database-per-tenant for 50k free users. No RLS backup when relying only on application code.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: automated tests inject wrong tenant_id and assert  zero rows returned; RLS enabled on all pooled tables; migration runbook tested quarterly.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Trusting developers to always add WHERE tenant_id — rejected. Strong answer: RLS + middleware + integration tests + code review.

interviewTakeaways: Row pool default; schema or DB per tenant for enterprise silo.
PostgreSQL RLS enforces tenant isolation at database layer.
DynamoDB: embed tenant_id in partition key design.
60s: Row-level for scale with RLS safety net. Schema/DB per tenant for silo. Test cross-tenant access fails. Migration runbook for tier upgrades.
Follow-up: RLS performance impact at scale?
commonPitfalls: No tenant filter in ORM query — data leak, interview failure.
Strong answer: RLS, middleware tenant context, automated isolation tests.
DB per tenant for all free users — cost kill.
RLS not enabled — single bug leaks all data.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Prisma $use middleware injects tenant_id filter on every query — app-layer RLS equivalent.
Repository pattern requiring TenantId parameter prevents unscoped queries at compile time.
